subject: EverUp DR SLA tolerance discussion (standby activation / RTO/RPO)
messages:
From: Samantha Ortiz <samantha@everup.com>
To: markus_klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
Cc: ops@everup.com
Date: 2026-10-25T14:07:00Z
Subject: DR SLA question — standby activation lead time

Hi Markus,

Thanks for the demo last week. We're getting the contract team and our security/compliance folks aligned and a couple of items popped up around standby activation windows and RTO tolerances. Our auditors are pushing back on a 15-minute activation SLA for multi-region failover because of change-control and some network peering approvals we need to coordinate across our regulated subsidiaries.

Practically speaking we need EverUp to request a carveout that allows a 60-minute warm-standby activation window for the primary analytics workload in the US region. We can accept a shorter RTO for customer-facing APIs (15 minutes) but want the analytics and batch processing to be treated as a separate class with a 60-minute activation tolerance and an RPO of 15 minutes.

I've attached our current failover runbook (EverUp_failover_runbook.pdf) for context. Can you confirm whether Redwood can support a split RTO/RPO by traffic class and whether you can put that in an addendum rather than changing the base SLA?

Best,
Samantha Ortiz
Head of Ops — EverUp Finance
attachments: EverUp_failover_runbook.pdf

From: markus_klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Ortiz <samantha@everup.com>
Cc: lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, irene_choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-26T09:12:00Z
Subject: Re: DR SLA question — standby activation lead time

Samantha — thanks for the context and the runbook.

Short answers up front: yes, we can support traffic-class based RTO/RPO in our routing+standby model; yes, we can do it via an addendum for the contract.

A few clarifying items so we scope the carveout correctly:
- Which VM/images are in the "analytics" class vs. "customer-facing APIs" (a short list of service names or logical routes will do).
- Is warm standby acceptable (we assume warm instances with warmed KV caches and prefix caching) or do you need fully hot active-active for analytics? Warm is what you'd describe above and is the more common carveout.
- For the 60-minute activation, do you require an automated failover trigger or will it be a manual activation initiated by EverUp SREs (we offer both; activation lead time differs slightly).

Proposed approach:
1) Formal addendum with two traffic classes: CORE_APIS (15min RTO / 1min RPO) and ANALYTICS_BATCH (60min RTO / 15min RPO).
2) Exception term: 12-month pilot after signature with quarterly readiness testing and a predefined runbook test on Day 30.
3) Reduced SLA credit for ANALYTICS_BATCH during the pilot window (we can propose a pro rata credit schedule).

I'll loop Legal for the addendum language and have Lauren draft commercial terms. Irene, can you confirm whether the proposed logging/audit retention (90 days for failover traces) meets our security requirements for an exception?

—Markus
Markus Klein
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference

From: Samantha Ortiz <samantha@everup.com>
To: markus_klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
Cc: ops@everup.com
Date: 2026-11-01T16:40:00Z
Subject: Re: DR SLA question — standby activation lead time

Thanks Markus — good to hear. Quick answers:
- Analytics services: batch-agg, billing-processor, ledger-reconcile, reports-worker (I'll send a short mapping doc later today).
- Warm standby is acceptable for analytics; we do need KV cache priming and warmed model containers within the warm pool so tokenized inference state recovers quickly.
- Activation will be a joint decision by EverUp SRE & Redwood ops; we'd like an automated option if downstream checks pass (i.e., health and peer-checks).

We're open to the 12-month pilot but will need the audit evidence for our compliance review (this is a hard ask). If you can commit to quarterly readiness tests and provide the evidence (logs + timestamps), we should be able to sign.

Also, we have a procurement milestone on Nov 12 — would Redwood be able to deliver a finalized addendum and commercial terms by Nov 9 so we can route to our procurement/legal?

—Samantha
Samantha Ortiz
Head of Ops — EverUp Finance

From: lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Ortiz <samantha@everup.com>
Cc: markus_klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>, irene_choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-03T11:06:00Z
Subject: Re: DR SLA question — standby activation lead time

Samantha — looping in commercial details as requested.

We can deliver a draft addendum and proposed commercial schedule by COB Nov 6 to meet your procurement milestone. High-level terms we intend to include:
- Scope: traffic-class carveout (CORE_APIS vs ANALYTICS_BATCH) defined by route tags and service names you provided.
- Term: 12-month carveout pilot, auto-review 90 days prior to expiry.
- Credits: for CORE_APIS we maintain standard SLA credits; for ANALYTICS_BATCH during the pilot we offer a capped credit (max 10% of monthly invoice) in lieu of stricter availability.
- Audit & evidence: Redwood will provide quarterly readiness reports with logs, activation timestamps, and can provide a signed PDF of each test.
- Termination: Either party can exit the carveout with 30 days' notice after the pilot.

I'll attach the proposed addendum draft and a readiness checklist — please note the addendum references a test matrix that we will run with your SREs.

Attachments: redwood_proposed-addendum_v1.docx; quarterly-readiness-checklist.xlsx

If these high-level terms look ok, I can send the formal DocuSign bundle on Nov 6.

Thanks,
Lauren Bishop
Enterprise Account Executive — Redwood Inference

From: markus_klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Ortiz <samantha@everup.com>, lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Cc: irene_choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-05T09:12:00Z
Subject: Re: DR SLA question — standby activation lead time

Samantha / Lauren — all sounds good. Next steps:
1) Lauren to send the DocuSign addendum package on Nov 6 (target).
2) EverUp to provide the short service mapping doc (analytics service list) by Nov 7 so we can bake exact route tags into the addendum.
3) Schedule a 60-minute ops readiness run on Nov 18 (we'll coordinate exact time) — this will satisfy the Day 30 test requirement for the pilot.

Irene confirmed 90-day log retention for failover traces meets our minimum for the exception. We'll capture the activation timestamps and share signed PDFs after each quarterly test.

We'll also include a simple fallback policy in the addendum: if activation exceeds 60 minutes for ANALYTICS_BATCH more than twice in a rolling 90-day window, Redwood will propose a remediation plan and a joint review with EverUp SREs.

Thanks — I'll mark the HubSpot deal HP-8342 and add the DocuSign link once sent.

—Markus
Markus Klein
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference
